THE RESULT: 65 of the 103 (63 per cent) are named in the paper at least once. 18 of the 103 (17 per cent) are certainly inside a printed photograph, meaning a caption names them. 6 of the 103 (6 per cent) are in a photograph where their own position can be proved and the face is legible, and those 6 are the portraits cut on this run. Put the other way: 38 of the 103 are not in the paper at any point in thirteen years of it, and of the 18 who were photographed, two thirds are unusable - a night silhouette, an overhead shot of the tops of two heads, a figure forty halftone dots wide across a road, a three-name crowd caption with no positions. The shape by cohort is steady: 70 per cent named in 1997-98, 66 per cent in 1998-99, 57 per cent in 2000-01. The 2001-02 cohort drops to 27 per cent, but those eleven were all sworn in between January and March 2002 and the digitised run thins after 2003, so that is a coverage artefact rather than a change in the paper. It makes no difference whether a member held a named seat or is known only from a roll call: 59 per cent of seat-holders and 69 per cent of roll-call names are in the paper.

name: WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE OTHER EIGHT BLOCKS
fact: On this evidence a dedicated rank-and-file pass over the roughly six hundred senators in the archive would be expected to return a portrait for about one in sixteen of them, near forty faces, at a cost of about one worked page per person. That is a real return and it is worth doing, but it should be planned as a numbers exercise and not as a per-person hunt: two thirds of the yield came from two sources that can be mined in bulk rather than name by name, the opinion-page poll strip and the spring SGA candidate profile page, and almost nothing came from reading news photographs one at a time. The single most useful thing a future pass can do first is build the poll-label index by GEOMETRY rather than by the words 'People Poll' (see the archive-gaps entry on this run), because the column outlived its own title and 1999-2004 is unindexed. The second is to pull every spring election issue and read the candidate pages, which print a studio head shot with the candidate's name in bold directly beneath it. Reading news pages for a named senator is the expensive route and it produced two usable faces out of about seventy pages opened.

name: Bryan Daniel
fact: FACE PROVED, PERSON NOT PROVED - FOR THE EDITOR. The Herald photographed a Bryan Daniel repeatedly and captioned him with a position, which is everything the identification rule asks for except the one thing that matters here. Cara VanLeuven's picture of 29 October 1998 reads 'Sophomore wide receiver Clarence Jackson, left, and senior corner back Bryan Daniel perform offensive [drills]', so the right-hand figure is provably Bryan Daniel; Barry Westerman's of 7 April 1998 and Carrie Pratt's of 7 May 1998 name him again, and a track report of 25 February 1999 has senior sprinter Bryan Daniel winning the 55-metre dash. All of these are the Hilltopper football and track man, a senior cornerback from Fort Lauderdale, Fla. NOTHING TIES HIM TO STUDENT GOVERNMENT. The Congress member was sworn in as an At-Large representative on 22 September 1998 and appears in the minutes of that meeting as 'Brian Daniel', which is a different spelling again. A senior in autumn 1998 could plausibly have taken an At-Large seat, and no second Bryan Daniel appears in the digitised Herald, but plausibility is not proof and the face has not been cut. If the editor can put the footballer in SGA from any source, the frame of 29 October 1998 is ready and the position is unambiguous.

name: J Thomas
kind: a frame exists that cannot be identified
fact: The People Poll of 11 November 1997, printed p. 4, carries a clean labelled mugshot of 'Jay Thomas, Bardstown sophomore', 322 pixels wide on a 2,211-pixel scan. The archive's 1997-98 Congress member is recorded only as the initial 'J Thomas', never with a first name, and a Bardstown sophomore in autumn 1997 is exactly the right cohort. It is NOT cut, because expanding an initial is not an identification: J could be Jay, James, Jason, Jeff, John or Jennifer, and nothing in any source puts Jay Thomas in student government. The frame is recorded here so a later pass with a fuller 1997-98 roster can settle it in one step rather than searching again.
